cards.q: Adult CICO after failed intubation. Which front-of-neck technique does DAS 2025 recommend?
options: Scalpel–bougie–tube through a vertical midline skin incision
cards.why: DAS 2025 keeps scalpel–bougie–tube for Plan D and makes a vertical midline skin incision the default for every patient.

cards.q: Which tube is railroaded over the bougie in adult scalpel cricothyroidotomy?
cards.why: A lubricated cuffed 6.0 mm tube fits the cricothyroid membrane and allows ventilation with a seal.

cards.q: How do you confirm a front-of-neck tube is in the trachea?
options: The chest rises when you bag
cards.why: Only waveform capnography confirms tracheal placement. A false passage can still move the chest.

cards.q: Chest drain for haemothorax. Which immediate output suggests the need for thoracotomy?
cards.why: Massive haemothorax: 1500 mL immediately, or ongoing 200 mL/h for 2–4 hours, needs surgical exploration.

cards.q: Adult tension pneumothorax. Where does ATLS 10th edition place needle decompression?
options: 4th/5th intercostal space, just anterior to the midaxillary line
cards.why: ATLS 10th moved the adult site to the 4th/5th ICS just anterior to the midaxillary line; the 2nd ICS midclavicular site stays for children.

cards.q: Where should a pelvic binder be centred?
cards.why: A binder over the greater trochanters closes the pelvic ring. Placed on the iliac crests it can open it.

cards.q: Penetrating torso trauma, no head injury, bleeding before surgical control. Typical systolic BP target?
options: No target: give 3 L crystalloid first
cards.why: Balanced (permissive) resuscitation accepts a lower systolic until the bleeding is controlled. Not with a head injury.

cards.q: Tranexamic acid in bleeding trauma. When should it be given?
options: Within 3 hours of injury: 1 g over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h
Only once the INR is back
cards.why: CRASH-2: benefit when given within 3 hours; after 3 hours it may harm.

cards.q: Adult thermal burn over 20% TBSA. ATLS 10th starting fluid formula?
options: 2 mL/kg/%TBSA crystalloid over 24 h, half in the first 8 h
4 mL/kg/%TBSA, all in the first 8 h
cards.why: ATLS 10th starts adults at 2 mL/kg/%TBSA (3 mL for children, 4 mL for electrical burns), then titrates to urine output. Older teaching (Parkland) uses 4 mL.
cards.note: Parkland is 4 mL/kg/%TBSA; ATLS 10th changed the adult starting rate to 2 mL/kg/%TBSA.

cards.q: Adult burn resuscitation. What urine output are you aiming for?
cards.why: Adults 0.5 mL/kg/h; children under 30 kg 1 mL/kg/h; electrical injury 1–1.5 mL/kg/h.

cards.q: Canadian C-spine rule. Which of these is a high-risk factor that mandates imaging?
options: Neck pain that came on later
cards.why: High-risk factors: age 65 or over, a dangerous mechanism, or paraesthesia in the limbs.

cards.q: Abnormal flexion (decorticate posturing) to pain scores what on the GCS motor scale?
cards.why: Motor: 6 obeys, 5 localises, 4 normal flexion/withdrawal, 3 abnormal flexion, 2 extension, 1 none.
